Herman Melville, Short Fiction, edited by Raymond Weaver.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/herman-melville/short-fiction

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Herman Melville, the annotator and the author, died 1891 (Wikidata Q4985, date of death 1891-09-28).
- Raymond Weaver, the editor, died 1948 (Wikidata Q3930690, date of death 1948-01-01).

First publication of the text used: between 1853 and 1856 (SE colophon: 'Short Fiction was compiled from short stories published between 1853 and 1856 by Herman Melville.').

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published between 1853 and 1856, before 1931. The edition's own statement of rights, quoted below, says the text is in the United States public domain.
- Country of origin: the possible countries of first publication are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Nothing in the facts points to France, Spain, Mexico, Colombia or Russia/USSR. The last person to die among those named above died in 1948, and each of these countries has a term of life + 70 years or less, so the work is public domain in each of them.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon: first publication between 1853 and 1856 (quoted above).
- Wikidata Q4985 (Herman Melville), P570 = 1891-09-28.
- Wikidata Q3930690 (Raymond Weaver), P570 = 1948-01-01.
